subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec-security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests preserve session defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make config the upper bound
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused migration or reset coverage.

options.title: Keep persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset or patch sessions to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Ship explicit reset first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make config the upper bound
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused migration or reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and tests points to steipete.
